name: Ameriprint Apparel
old_description: Custom Screen Printing for Schools, Teams & Corporate Apparel
about:
Ameriprint Apparel has operated from Sun Prairie, Wisconsin since 1985. The shop serves the Madison metro area and runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. No founder names or ownership structure are publicly disclosed.

The company provides custom decoration services including screen printing for vibrant, durable bulk orders; embroidery for uniforms and promotional items; direct-to-film (DTF) and digital printing for full-color, on-demand designs on cotton and cotton-blend fabrics; and laser engraving on drinkware, awards, leather, and acrylic. It also sources promotional products such as tote bags, drinkware, pens, and headwear, and offers inventory storage and fulfillment for client webstores. All production occurs in-house at the Sun Prairie facility.

Customers range from schools and sports teams to corporate buyers, event organizers, and non-profit groups. Recent orders highlighted in reviews include team apparel for a Lithuanian dance festival, shirts for an American Legion post, fraternity t-shirts, and family reunion tops. The business also handles trade-show giveaways, employee onboarding kits, and holiday corporate gifts.

Ameriprint emphasizes its in-house graphics team and an online design tool that lets customers create or refine artwork. The company also promotes inventory storage and fulfillment as a way to streamline recurring orders, and notes that it can accommodate small orders alongside large runs.

name: Amphenol DC Electronics
old_description: 70,000 sq ft facility making custom cable/wire harness assemblies (Amphenol division)
about:
Amphenol DC Electronics, based in San Jose, California, was founded in 1979 by David Cianciulli after he left Hughes Aircraft. The company was acquired by Amphenol in 2013 and operates as a division of that global interconnect manufacturer.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures custom wire harnesses, cable assemblies, and integrated electronic mechanical devices (box builds). Its services include overmolded cable assemblies, discrete assemblies, and value‑added services such as in‑house tooling, lean manufacturing, and engineering liaison. Production takes place in a 70,000‑square‑foot facility in Silicon Valley, with additional manufacturing sites in Nogales, Mexico, and Malaysia.

Amphenol DC Electronics serves medical device manufacturers (MRI, CT, X‑ray, patient monitoring, surgical robotics), aerospace and military customers (including Trimble for handheld GPS during the Gulf War), defense contractors, industrial equipment makers (factory automation robotics), and precision agriculture equipment producers. The company holds ISO 13485:2016 for medical, ITAR registration, and IPC‑620 Class III certification for electronic assemblies.

The company emphasizes its singular focus on custom cable and wire harness assemblies for over 30 years, which it says provides deep expertise to identify design and manufacturability issues early. It highlights continual improvement, lean practices across information and material flow, in‑house engineering and design liaison for build‑to‑print proficiency, and personalized customer support with prompt order fulfillment.

name: Amphenol TPC Wire & Cable
old_description: Can’t seem to find a standard solution for your connector or cable needs?
about:
Amphenol TPC Wire & Cable is headquartered in Macedonia, Ohio. The company traces its origins to 1979 when it began supplying high-performance wire and cable engineered for harsh industrial environments. No founders are named in public sources, and the ownership structure beyond the Amphenol branding is not detailed.

The company manufactures and supplies a range of products including wire, cable, connectors, cable assemblies, cable management systems, cordsets, and electrical components. It also offers custom-engineered solutions designed by an in-house team of electrical, industrial, and mechanical engineers. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are publicly disclosed.

Amphenol TPC serves a broad set of industries: automotive, food and beverage, general manufacturing, industrial automation, metals, mining, oil and gas, rail and transit, shipyard and marine, utility and power transmission, and wood, pulp, and paper. Customer testimonials cite applications in welding operations, freezer environments, and shipyard welding cable installations.

The company emphasizes its role as a problem-solver, providing abuse-resistant cables that withstand abrasion, chemicals, extreme temperatures, flexing, impact, and tension. A noted case study reports a shipyard saving $286,000 over two years by switching to the company's Super-Trex® 600 Volt Welding Cable.

name: Ampleon USA Inc.
old_description: The advent of 5G NR (New Radio) since 2019 has ushered in a new era with demanding prerequisites for RF power components. Ampleon stands at the forefront, providing market leading RF power solutions for mMIMO (Massive Multiple Input Multiple Output) of up to 128 simultaneous transmit and receive streams, high efficiency small cell, and high-power macro base stations.
about:
Ampleon USA Inc. maintains a sales and engineering office in Smithfield, Rhode Island, as part of the global Ampleon organization headquartered in Nijmegen, Netherlands. The company operates a dedicated production facility in Cabuyao, Philippines, and holds additional sales offices across China, Finland, France, Korea, Sweden, Taiwan, and a second U.S. location in Dallas, Texas.

The company designs and manufactures RF power transistors, including gallium-nitride-on-silicon-carbide (GaN-on-SiC) HEMT devices and silicon LDMOS discrete transistors. These components serve 5G New Radio infrastructure such as massive MIMO arrays with up to 128 simultaneous streams, high-efficiency small cells, and high-power macro base stations. Ampleon also supplies solid-state RF generators for particle accelerators and industrial heating applications, with power levels ranging from kilowatts to megawatts.

Ampleon’s customer base spans telecommunications equipment makers, industrial and scientific research facilities, and medical technology manufacturers. The company’s distribution network covers the Americas, EMEA, South Asia Pacific, Japan, China, and Korea, supported by a team of manufacturer’s representatives covering all 50 U.S. states and international distributors.

Ampleon emphasizes its focus on high-efficiency, high-power RF solutions that enable the transition from vacuum-tube to solid-state technology in particle acceleration and industrial heating, while delivering the density and performance required for advanced 5G base station architectures.

name: Amsted Automotive
old_description: Amsted Automotive Honored with Manufacturer of the Year – Large Tier & Manufacturing Export Product of the Year -
about:
Amsted Automotive, headquartered in Saginaw, Michigan, was formed in 2021 through the integration of Burgess-Norton (established 1903) and Means Industries (established 1922), along with Transform Automotive (1997) and SMW Manufacturing (2004). The combined entity operates 21 facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The company designs and manufactures high-performance components for vehicle and industrial applications, including brackets, welded assemblies, coupler components, piston pins, bearing products, wear parts, and powertrain components. Core processes include cold forming, powder metallurgy, advanced metal forming (flow forming, in-die spline forming, grob forming, laser welding, stamping), and propulsion systems (torque management, clutch technologies). With over 2,000 employees across 21 facilities worldwide (13 in the U.S.), Amsted produces more than 200 million components annually.

Amsted serves global automotive, off-highway, mining, and industrial markets. Its components are used in electric heavy-duty e-axles, wheel-end bolts and hubs, traditional and hybrid powertrains, brake systems, electric drivelines, chassis and suspension systems, fluid conveyance, and industrial cutting tools. Customers include automakers and Tier 1 suppliers seeking flexible manufacturing across internal combustion, hybrid, and electric propulsion architectures.

The company emphasizes its regional manufacturing footprint—13 U.S. facilities plus global sites—to mitigate tariff risks and supply delays, enabling production close to customer demand. Its integration of legacy brands brings together cold forming, powder metallurgy, and advanced metal forming expertise to deliver tailored, high-quality components for evolving propulsion technologies.

Anchorage Sheet Metal emphasizes its licensed, bonded, and insured workforce, HVAC certification, and competitive pricing as key differentiators in the regional market, positioning itself as a single-source provider for both fabrication and mechanical contracting needs.

name: Andersen Industries, Inc.
old_description: Large custom walk-in sheet-metal enclosures and control houses
about:
Andersen Industries, Inc. was founded in 1966 in Adelanto, California, beginning as a small backyard welding repair shop. Over nearly six decades, the company has grown into a 108,000-square-foot purpose-built facility equipped with overhead cranes and designed for heavy fabrication.

The company provides end-to-end metal manufacturing services, including sheet metal fabrication, CNC laser cutting, turret punching, plasma cutting, sawing, press brake forming, plate rolling, CNC milling and turning, welding, finishing, and assembly. It also designs and manufactures its own line of WeldPro 360 MIG welding boom arms and fume extraction systems. In-house capabilities span from 3D CAD engineering through to finished product delivery.

Andersen serves manufacturers and OEMs across industries such as retail merchandising, food services, commercial and industrial vehicles, and oil and gas. Its customer base also includes specialty equipment manufacturers, machine tool builders, and contractors seeking single-source fabrication of brackets, cabinets, enclosures, frames, tanks, weldments, and custom control houses.

The company emphasizes its five decades of experience, purpose-built facility, and advanced equipment as the foundation for delivering high-quality, durable components on time and within budget. Its proprietary welding boom systems are engineered to minimize non-arc time and maximize operator productivity, reflecting a focus on improving customer performance and profitability.

about:
Andersen Manufacturing Inc., doing business as Andersen Hitches, is a family-owned manufacturer based in Idaho Falls, Idaho. Founded in 1948, the company began as a single-room shop and has remained under family ownership for generations.

Today the firm operates a 102,000-square-foot manufacturing and fabrication complex that was expanded by an additional 70,000 square feet in 2021. It produces a full line of trailer hitches—including fifth-wheel connections, bumper-pull hitches, weight-distribution systems—and a range of trailer accessories such as jack blocks, levelers, locking pins, and the Rapid Pin one-hand hitch pin. Products are built from steel and aluminum and carry a lifetime warranty on nearly every item.

Andersen serves the towing industry, supplying recreational travelers, commercial haulers, and outdoor enthusiasts through a nationwide network of authorized dealers. Its hitches and accessories are designed for everything from light-duty bumper-pull trailers to heavy fifth-wheel RVs.

The company emphasizes original, patent-pending designs that aim to make towing setup faster, cleaner, and easier—highlighting innovations like the lightweight Ultimate 5th Wheel Connection and the Rapid Jack tire-changing accessory.

name: Anderson Electric Co.
old_description: We value a long lasting relationship with each and every client.
about:
Anderson Electric Co. was founded in 2020 in Aberdeen, South Dakota, by Shaine Anderson. A family‑owned electrical contracting firm, it traces its roots to Anderson’s start in the trade at the end of 2005. He spent nearly six years with a local contractor learning residential, commercial, and street‑lighting work, then helped construct the Aberdeen beef plant where he gained experience with 480 V switchgear and low‑voltage control systems. After the plant closed, he returned to construction and service work before joining the new plant owners to oversee electrical and fabrication‑floor maintenance departments for more than five years. Seeing a need for healthier client relationships and stronger workplace leadership, Anderson launched his own company built on the values of integrity, quality, and service.

The company designs, installs, repairs, and maintains electrical systems across residential, commercial, farm, and industrial sectors. Specialized services include industrial electrical maintenance, industrial project design, controls and automation, custom lighting projects, and smart‑home technology integration. All installed equipment is UL listed, and the firm is licensed, insured, and bonded in South Dakota with reciprocity in other states.

Anderson Electric serves homeowners, businesses, agricultural operations, and industrial facilities in and around Aberdeen. Recent projects cited by customers include converting a 1950s church into a café with modern lighting and kitchen outlets, installing bathroom‑fan ducting and wiring, updating wiring in older homes, and providing industrial maintenance for a beef‑processing plant. The firm also works with general contractors on new construction and renovation projects.

The company says its differentiation lies in its core values—integrity (no cutting corners, UL‑listed equipment), quality (exceeding code requirements), and service (vetted employees, “extra mile” attitude). Anderson also emphasizes a purpose‑driven model: each month the business donates to organizations such as Destiny Rescue, Coffee with a Cause, and Aberdeen’s Safe Harbor, linking its commercial work to community impact.

name: Andon Electronics Corporation
old_description: Andon Electronics Corporation - Innovative Socket Designs For Optimum Device Protection
about:
Andon Electronics Corporation is based in Lincoln, Rhode Island. The company is led by John O. Tate, who serves as president and is credited as the developer of the precision semiconductor socket contact. No founding year or ownership details are provided.

Andon manufactures innovative precision sockets used to place image sensors, optoelectronic sensors, gas sensors, DC-DC converters, batteries, crystal oscillators, fuses, relays, and other electronic devices onto printed circuit boards. The product line includes sockets categorized by device type—such as image sensor, optoelectronic sensor, gas sensor, power converter, crystal oscillator, battery, fuse, and display—and by package type, including PGA, BGA, LCC, DIP (closed and open frame), SIP, transistor outline (TO), PLCC, and LED. Specialty offerings encompass Heat Sink Sockets™, high-temperature sockets, terminals, test jacks, ultra-low profile sockets, floating pin sockets, and laminate wafer sockets without circuitry. The company provides both standard and custom socket solutions.

Andon’s sockets are used by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and contract manufacturers (CMs) across sectors such as camera production, laser manufacturing, and gas sensing equipment. Named customers in the company’s records include Chungwa Telecom Labs and Micropac Industries. OEMs and CMs adopt Andon sockets to avoid device damage, reduce board assembly labor, and improve turnaround times.

The company emphasizes its innovative socket designs for optimum device protection, a capability rooted in Tate’s development of the precision semiconductor socket contact. This focus on protecting sensitive components during assembly and streamlining the manufacturing process is presented as its core differentiator.
